warning: Red outlines are RIDEM’s own restricted waterfowl areas, from its Outdoor Recreation map. Amber marks places that stay open but carry conditions — shoot toward open water, or carry a way to retrieve. An amber circle is an approximate locator; an amber outline is the river, town or management area the rule names. National wildlife refuges have their own rules (Refuges layer), and town ordinances can add more.
source: RIDEM Outdoor Recreation map; Rhode Island Hunting and Trapping Regulations §9.11(G)–(H), 2026–27.

areas.n: Seekonk River — shoot toward open water
areas.d: On the Seekonk River outside the closed stretch, shoot only toward open water (seaward) while waterfowl hunting. The closed stretch (red) runs from the railroad bridge north to the Gulf Road – Omega Pond line. Outline: the river’s water from Fox Point up to Pawtucket Falls (USGS NHD).

The one stretch of the Barrington River open to hunting: east of Puritan Avenue (41.745873, −71.309876) and west of the point southwest of Seabrook Court (41.744189, −71.306622). Hunt only on the water below the vegetation line, and shoot only toward open water.
Walker Island, Bristol: shoot only toward open water (seaward) while waterfowl hunting.
Rock Island and the groin running north from it off Narragansett Parkway, Warwick: shoot only toward open water (seaward) while waterfowl hunting.

From Washouset Point (Pawtuxet Cove) north to Fields Point, including Stillhouse Cove: shoot only toward open water (seaward). No hunting from the shoreline or from a boat within 500 feet of an occupied building.
Anywhere in East Providence: shoot only toward open water (seaward) while waterfowl hunting, and check the city’s ordinances, which add restrictions.

areas.n: Little Compton — carry a way to retrieve
areas.d: Every waterfowl hunter in Little Compton must have a way to retrieve birds — a retrieving dog or a non-motorized boat, for example.

areas.n: Great Swamp — carry a way to retrieve
areas.d: Every waterfowl hunter at Great Swamp must have a way to retrieve birds — a retrieving dog or a non-motorized boat, for example.

Closed to waterfowl hunting: the Seekonk River north of the railroad bridge, up to a line from Gulf Road at River Drive (Providence) to the southern abutment of the railroad bridge at the outlet of Omega Pond (East Providence). Elsewhere on the Seekonk, shoot only toward open water (seaward).
Closed to waterfowl hunting — Mill Cove in its entirety, including the beachfront.
Closed to waterfowl hunting — Brush Neck Cove in its entirety.
Closed to waterfowl hunting — Buttonwoods Cove in its entirety.
Closed to waterfowl hunting — Mill Cove, Wickford, in its entirety.
Closed to waterfowl hunting west of the line the Division of Fish and Wildlife sets across Cornelius Island. East of it, shoot only in an easterly direction.

Closed to waterfowl hunting — the unnamed estuary north of Seapowet Avenue and east of Jack’s Island, bordered by the Audubon Society’s Emilie Ruecker Wildlife Refuge, including its inlet and the marsh on the north side of the outlet, as posted.
No firearm discharge in the Blackstone Valley flood plains and marshes (the “Valley Marshes”) — state law, R.I. Gen. Laws § 11-47-49.1.
Closed to all hunting — the shoreline between mean high and mean low water around Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge.
Closed to waterfowl hunting — Watchaug Pond and Poquiant Brook, and within 100 yards upland of their shores or banks.

Closed between Central Bridge (Massasoit Avenue) and Barrington Bridge #123 (County Road), except the stretch east of Puritan Avenue (41.745873, −71.309876) and west of the point southwest of Seabrook Court (41.744189, −71.306622). In that stretch: on the water below the vegetation line only, shooting toward open water.

Waterfowl hunting only in the signed northwest part of the large pond, and only after November 15 (town ordinance). Shoot toward open water; keep firearms cased until you reach your blind or boat. The red area is closed.
